facts.fact_text: The applicant was born in 1943.
The applicant lived in Budapest.
On 24 November 2006, the applicant announced to the Budapest Police Department his intention to organise a demonstration on 9 December 2006 on Kossuth Square in Budapest, in front of Parliament.
The announcement of 24 November 2006 was made as required by the Assembly Act 1989.
On 24 November 2006, the applicant announced to the Budapest Police Department his intention to organise a demonstration on 9 December 2006 on Kossuth Square in Budapest, in front of Parliament.
On 26 November 2006, the Budapest Police Department refused to deal with the applicant's application to organise a demonstration on Kossuth Square.
On 23 October 2006, the Budapest Police Department declared the area of Kossuth Square a 'security operational zone' (biztonsági műveleti terület) for an indefinite period of time.
The Budapest Police Department declared Kossuth Square a 'security operational zone' in view of the tumultuous events in Budapest in September 2006.

The Budapest Police Department observed that the designation of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone' placed it outside the Budapest Police Department's jurisdiction as regards the prohibition of, or acquiescence in, a demonstration.
On 6 December 2006, the Budapest Regional Court dismissed the applicant's request for judicial review of the Budapest Police Department's refusal to deal with the application.

The Budapest Regional Court, in dismissing the applicant's request for judicial review on 6 December 2006, observed that no decision on the merits of the case had ever been adopted by the administrative authorities, which excluded such a review.
On 11 December 2006, the Deputy Head of the National Police Department dismissed the applicant's further complaint.
On 19 December 2006, the applicant filed an action with the Budapest Regional Court challenging the decision of 23 October 2006 declaring Kossuth Square a 'security operational zone'.
On 19 December 2006, the applicant filed an action with the Budapest Regional Court challenging the decision of 11 December 2006 by the Deputy Head of the National Police Department.
On 11 January 2007, the Head of Budapest Police dismissed the applicant's renewed complaint.
On 12 February 2007, the Deputy Head of the National Police Department partly reversed the Head of Budapest Police's decision of 11 January 2007.

On 12 February 2007, the Deputy Head of the National Police Department instructed the Budapest Police Department to substitute the indefinite 'security operational zone' measure with one of definite duration.
On 5 March 2007, the Budapest Regional Court dismissed the applicant's action arising from the decisions of 11 January 2007 and 12 February 2007.
In dismissing the applicant's action on 5 March 2007, the Budapest Regional Court essentially endorsed the police authorities' earlier reasoning.

The Budapest Regional Court pointed out on 5 March 2007 that the proceedings only concerned the police's decision on non-competence and did not constitute a review of the police's original decision declaring Kossuth Square a 'security operational zone'.
Upon a further complaint by the applicant, on 18 March 2008 the Budapest Regional Court quashed the decisions of 11 January 2007 and 12 February 2007.
On 18 March 2008, the Budapest Regional Court remitted the case to the National Police Department.
In reaction to the applicant's petition for review, on 29 April 2009 the Supreme Court quashed the Budapest Regional Court's decision of 18 March 2008.
On 29 April 2009, the Supreme Court remitted the case to the Budapest Regional Court.
The Budapest Regional Court's procedure was interrupted on 1 October 2009 on account of the applicant's death.
The applicant's son and heir joined the proceedings before the Budapest Regional Court as successor on 25 August 2011.

The Government submitted that the subject matter of the litigation pending before the Budapest Regional Court was the police's original decision declaring Kossuth Square a 'security operational zone'.
In a case concerning the same area (Kossuth Square), on 29 January 2007 a Mr K. challenged the police's decision to declare Kossuth Square a 'security operational zone'.
On 14 March 2007, the Budapest Police Commander rejected Mr K.'s complaint challenging the declaration of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone'.
The Budapest Police Commander's decision of 14 March 2007 rejecting Mr K.'s complaint was quashed by the National Commander on 16 April 2007.

In the resumed administrative proceedings, on 22 June 2007 the Budapest Police Commander again rejected Mr K.'s complaint challenging the declaration of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone'.
On 19 July 2007, the National Commander upheld the Budapest Police Commander's decision of 22 June 2007 rejecting Mr K.'s complaint.
Mr K. challenged the National Commander's ruling of 19 July 2007 in court.
Mr K.'s action challenging the National Commander's ruling of 19 July 2007 was dismissed by the Budapest Regional Court.
On appeal, the Supreme Court quashed the Budapest Regional Court's decision dismissing Mr K.'s action.
On appeal, the Supreme Court quashed the National Commander's decision of 19 July 2007.

In the resumed second-instance administrative proceedings, on 23 December 2009 the National Commander again upheld the Budapest Police Commander's decision rejecting Mr K.'s complaint about the declaration of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone'.
Mr K. requested judicial review of the National Commander's decision of 23 December 2009.

On 11 November 2010, the Budapest Regional Court issued judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9., quashing both the first-instance and the second-instance administrative decisions concerning the declaration of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone'.
On 11 November 2010, the Budapest Regional Court remitted the case to the Budapest Police Commander.

The Budapest Regional Court in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9. pointed out that the impugned administrative decisions did not contain any concrete elements establishing the necessity and proportionality of maintaining the 'security operational zone' after the prolongation of 22 November 2006.

The Budapest Regional Court in judgment no. 27.K.31.354/2010/9. pointed out that the impugned administrative decisions did not address Mr K.'s suggestion that the mere fencing-off of Parliament's immediate vicinity, rather than the global ban on Kossuth Square, would have been sufficient in the circumstances.

In the resumed first-instance administrative proceedings, on 4 April 2011 the Budapest Police Commander partly sustained Mr K.'s complaint concerning the declaration of Kossuth Square as a 'security operational zone'.

On 4 April 2011, the Budapest Police Commander noted that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, the proportionality of the 'security operational zone' measure had successfully been challenged by Mr K.
